1  HON'BLE ANIL KUMAR-X, J.
1. Heard learned counsel for appellant and learned AGA for the State.
2. Learned AGA states that notice has been served on opposite party no. 2, however, none has appeared on behalf of opposite party no.2 to oppose the appeal.
Copy of the notice provided by the learned AGA be kept on record.

3. This criminal appeal under Section 14-A(2) of The Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 has been preferred by the appellant with a prayer to allow the appeal, set aside the bail rejection order dated 03.07.2025 passed by Court Special Judge SC/ST Act,
Kushinagar at Padrauna, and to release the appellant on bail in Case Crime No.101 of 2025 Under Section 376, 504, 506 IPC, and Section 3 (1) Dha, SC/ST Act, Police Station-Khadda, District Kushinagar.

sentences.text: 4. Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that it is admitted fact by the prosecution that victim and the appellant were in consensual relations for past six years.
However, certain dispute arose between them and consequently an FIR with false allegation of committing rape on the pretext of marriage has been lodged by the victim.

Entire version of the first information and the statement of victim recorded during the investigation is nothing but an attempt to falsely implicate the appellant only because the relation between the parties turned sour.
The appellant has not committed any offence.
It was submitted that the impugned order rejecting the bail application of the appellant suffers from infirmity and illegality warranting interference by this Court.
In such circumstances, the appellant is entitled to bail.
5. Learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the prayer for bail and has submitted that the appellant is not entitled to bail.
6. I have considered the rival submissions so made and have gone through the entire record.

7. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, the Court is of the opinion that the appellant has made out a case for bail.
8. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed and the impugned order rejecting the bail application of the appellant is set-aside.
Pending application, if any, shall stand disposed of.

9. Let the appellant- Mahesh Pal, involved in the aforesaid case be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The appellant will not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
(ii) The appellant will not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witness.

(v) The appellant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
